name: r3-external-1
statement: The temperature sensitivity of the cued base and of RL-Zero-Math 3.0 and the insensitivity of 3.1 are one mechanism: sampling a pretrained-style policy with an over-truncated sampler (T < 1 or top-p/min-p) drops it into self-reinforcing repetition basins (Holtzman), and 3.1's recipe of training cap-truncated rollouts as negatives, with rollouts drawn by an exact T 1.0 sampler so the sign law gives no entropy drift, pushes down exactly the trajectories that enter those basins without making the policy flatter; 3.0, which masked truncations, keeps the basins and so behaves like the base under temperature.
scope: Covers Olmo-3-1025-7B base (cued and plain), Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math (step 2,800), Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math (3.0 release) and the Code-RL 3.0/3.1 pair, on MATH-500 and the clean hard328 with a 16,384-token cap, comparing T 0.6/top-p 0.95, T 0.6/top-p 1.0, T 1.0 with or without min-p/top-p, and T 1.5 + min-p. It explains cap hits, rule-A loops and the temperature dependence of accuracy. It does NOT explain the ~10.6-point MATH-500 gap or the 12.8-point hard328 gap that remain at T 1.0, where neither model loops (those are finished-wrong answers and non-loop cap hits). It assumes Olmo's RL rollouts were sampled at T 1.0 without truncation (to be checked in open-instruct); if the rollout sampler was truncated, the sign law predicts 3.1 should be the higher-entropy model and the second offline prediction flips.

imports.finding: Temperature sampling repeats unless very high temperatures are used, and any stochastic decoder whose parameters over-truncate the tail degenerates into repetitive loops, mimicking greedy search.
imports.how: Supplies the loop basin: for a policy that has not been trained against long repetitive trajectories, low T or tail truncation raises the probability of entering a self-reinforcing repeat and running to the cap; T 1.0 without truncation (or T 1.5 + min-p) escapes it.

imports.finding: With truncated rollout samplers a constant advantage shift changes entropy at first order (Mask vs Fail of over-length rollouts drift -21.3 under truncation) but only +0.7 under exact sampling; the choice between masking and failing truncated rollouts sets the released policy's entropy in a predictable direction.
imports.how: Separates the two effects of 3.1's 'truncated = negative' recipe: under an exact T 1.0 rollout sampler it adds no entropy drift, so its first-order effect is to lower the probability of cap-running (looping) trajectories; 3.0's masking left those trajectories unpenalised, so 3.0 inherits the base's loop basin and temperature sensitivity.

explains.how: T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 is the over-truncated regime in which the base enters repetition basins.
Removing top-p but keeping T 0.6 still truncates the effective distribution, so loops fall only partly.

explains.quote: Truncating the tail at T 1.0 brings loops back
explains.how: Tail truncation alone (min-p 0.1, top-p 0.95) re-creates the over-truncated regime at T 1.0, as the Holtzman mechanism requires.

explains.quote: T 1.5 + min-p 0.1 removes them (0 loops, 29 cap)
explains.how: A higher temperature re-flattens the head enough that the truncated sampler no longer collapses into repeats.

explains.quote: At T 1.0 rule A finds 0 loops in T1, T2 and T3
explains.how: Exact T 1.0 sampling is outside the loop regime for every model.
3.1 was trained to avoid cap-running trajectories, so lowering T no longer opens loop basins and accuracy is unchanged.
The extra 11.4 points of gap at T 0.6 are the base's loop losses, which 3.1 does not suffer.
The same escape from repetition basins at T 1.0 holds on the harder set.

explains.quote: not masking truncated sequences (they are trained as negatives)
explains.how: This is the recipe difference that, under an exact sampler, penalises loop trajectories in 3.1 and not in 3.0.
3.0 at T 0.6 sits at the cued base's T 0.6 level, as expected if it keeps the base's loop basin.
The masked-truncation 3.0 Code model loops heavily at T 0.8 while 3.1 Code does not.
The 3.0 RL-Zero-Math model at T 0.6 hits the length limit even more than the base: masking did not remove the basin.

conflicts.quote: Rule-A loops: 0 of 500 in either cell
conflicts.how: At T 1.0 neither model loops yet RL still leads by 10.6 points, so the remaining gap is outside this mechanism.

conflicts.quote: RL: T 1.0 - T 0.6 -0.4 overall, cap hits -8.0 points in Q4
conflicts.how: 3.1 still gains cap hits at T 0.6 on the longest problems, so its loop suppression is not complete; the theory needs those extra RL cap hits to be mostly non-loop long reasoning.
If tail truncation were the main lever, dropping top-p at T 0.6 should recover more than an uncertain 4.8 points; temperature itself must carry most of the effect.

rival: RL 3.1 is temperature-insensitive simply because RL sharpens any policy (low per-token entropy, so T 0.6 vs 1.0 hardly changes the samples), with no role for how truncated rollouts were trained. The separating observation is RL-Zero-Math 3.0 (masked truncations, similar RL length): the rival predicts it is also temperature-insensitive with few cap hits at T 0.6, while this theory predicts 3.0 loops at T 0.6 (cap hits above 15 % of MATH-500, most of them rule-A loops) and gains several points from T 0.6 to T 1.0. A second separator: under the rival the RL's few T 0.6 cap hits are loops like the base's; under this theory they are mostly non-repetitive long reasoning.

predictions.experiment: allenai/Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math (3.0 release, main dee26a40) with its own tokenizer and chat template, plain prompt, MATH-500 problems 0-249, one sample, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, cap 16,384, vLLM, seeds 1,000,000 + i; count cap hits.
predictions.refuted_by: Fewer than 20 cap hits of 250 (3.0 does not loop at T 0.6), or fewer than half of its cap hits flagged by rule A.

predictions.experiment: Same 3.0 model, same 250 problems and prompt, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, seeds 1,000,000 + i, grader v3; report right of 250 and compare with the T 0.6 cell above.
predictions.refuted_by: T 1.0 minus T 0.6 for 3.0 is at or below +1.0 point on these 250 (3.0 as temperature-insensitive as 3.1), or T 1.0 cap hits are not at least halved relative to T 0.6.

predictions.experiment: Offline: share of the RL model's T 0.6 cap hits on the clean hard328 that are repetition loops.
predictions.recipe: File s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s2800-01/out/P_hard.jsonl (RL step 2,800, plain, T 0.6/top-p 0.95). Keep rows whose problem is unflagged in results/rln3/rln3_overlap.json (the clean 328); if a problem has several rows keep sample 0. Select rows with cap_hit true. For each, apply rule A: for every start position p that is 0 or the index right after a '\n' in text, with len(text) - p >= 8,000 characters, take w = text[p:p+8000] encoded UTF-8 and compute len(zlib.compress(w)) / len(w) with Python zlib default level; the row is a loop if any window gives < 0.10. Statistic = loops / cap-hit rows. If there are no cap-hit rows, report NA (counts as not refuting).
predictions.unit: fraction of RL cap hits that are rule-A loops
predictions.refuted_by: A fraction above 0.45 (RL's T 0.6 cap hits are mostly loops, like the base's).

predictions.experiment: Offline: share of the cued base's T 0.6 cap hits on the clean hard328 that are repetition loops (the over-truncation basin on the harder set).
predictions.recipe: File s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/F_hard.jsonl (base, cue, T 0.6/top-p 0.95). Keep rows unflagged in results/rln3/rln3_overlap.json (clean 328), sample 0 only. Select rows with cap_hit true. Apply rule A exactly as in the previous recipe (line-start 8,000-character windows, zlib default level, ratio < 0.10). Statistic = loops / cap-hit rows.
predictions.unit: fraction of base cap hits that are rule-A loops
predictions.refuted_by: A fraction below 0.45 (most base T 0.6 cap hits on hard problems are not loops), which would leave the T 0.6 -> T 1.0 gain on hard328 unexplained by the loop basin.

predictions.experiment: Offline: per-token entropy of each model on its own MATH-500 answers at T 1.0 (3.1 should not be the flatter model under an exact rollout sampler).
predictions.recipe: File studies/rlneurons/results/rln5/map-01/checks.json, key per_row, lists T1 (base text, scored under base as own) and T2 (RL text, scored under RL as own). E_T1 = sum over all T1 rows of sum_entropy_own divided by sum over T1 rows of n_own; E_T2 likewise over T2 rows. Use all 500 rows of each list, cap hits included. Statistic = E_T2 / E_T1.
predictions.unit: ratio of RL to base mean per-token entropy (own text, own model)
predictions.refuted_by: A ratio above 1.05 (3.1 is the higher-entropy model, which the sign law gives only if rollouts were drawn with a truncated sampler).
